name: What is the best way to phase a renovation if I have a limited budget?

mainEntity.name: If my budget is limited, how should I phase a whole-home renovation without wasting money?
mainEntity.text: If my budget is limited, how should I phase a whole-home renovation without wasting money?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most important rule for phased work is to avoid doing low-value cosmetic updates before the major decisions are set. Start by fixing any structural issues, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, and layout problems that would be expensive to undo later. Then prioritize spaces that most affect daily life, usually the kitchen, primary bath, and key living areas. Save highly decorative or easily replaceable items for later phases. A phased approach works best when the entire project has a master plan so each step supports the next one. Without that plan, homeowners often spend money twice by completing finishes that later have to be removed or changed.
acceptedAnswer.description: If budget is limited, phase the project in a way that protects the big-picture plan. Start with structural, system, and layout decisions first, then complete the most lived-in spaces, and leave cosmetic items that can easily be finished later.
